# Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level

Coordinate `EN-103-000-0000-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M3-C-TO-H-0164` | `PM-069.1` | status ACTIVE | original slug `Global-quantum-geometric-Langlands-at-irrational-level-October-4-2026` | date 2026-10-04 | derived from the openai/math preprint Global-quantum-geometric-Langlands-at-irrational-level-October-4-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove the unramified quantum geometric Langlands equivalence for every connected simple complex algebraic group <i>G</i> and every level $`c\\in\\mathbb C\\setminus\\mathbb Q`$, including non-real levels. For every smooth projective connected complex curve <i>X</i>, it identifies the full twisted <i>D</i>-module categories on $`\\mathop{\\mathrm{Bun}}\\nolimits _G(X)`$ and $`\\mathop{\\mathrm{Bun}}\\nolimits _{G^\\vee}(X)`$ at the dual shifted levels <i>c</i> and $`-1/(rc)`$, where <i>r</i> is the lacing number. The equivalence uses the given global forms and includes all connected components.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove the unramified quantum geometric Langlands equivalence for every connected simple complex algebraic group <i>G</i> and every level $`c\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q`$, including non-real levels. For every smooth projective connected complex curve <i>X</i>, it identifies the full twisted <i>D</i>-module categories on $`\mathop{\mathrm{Bun}}\nolimits _G(X)`$ and $`\mathop{\mathrm{Bun}}\nolimits _{G^\vee}(X)`$ at the dual shifted levels <i>c</i> and $`-1/(rc)`$, where <i>r</i> is the lacing number. The equivalence uses the given global forms and includes all connected components.

- **claim-unramified-quantum-equivalence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): For every $c\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q$ there is an equivalence of presentable $\mathbb C$-linear DG categories $$\label{intro:equivalence} D_c(\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)) \simeq D_{-1/(rc)}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G^\vee}(X)).$$ The construction uses the given global forms and all connected components. It is characterized by the localization–Whittaker comparison of Section <a href="#sec:equivalence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:equivalence">13</a>, including its compatibility with families of marked points and their collisions. It also intertwines central torsor actions with the corresponding transgression local systems.
  - Explanation: Identifies the full twisted bundle categories at negative reciprocal shifted levels, retaining the actual global forms, components, family comparisons, and central actions.
- **claim-inertia-vanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-foundations-inertia)): Let $Z$ be an algebraic stack carrying a line $L$. Suppose a central $\mathbb G_m$ in its inertia acts on $L$ with a fixed nonzero integral weight $m$. If $sm\notin\mathbb Z$, then $D_Z(L^s)=0$. The assertion remains valid after restricting to a locally closed substack and after taking a product with a spectator stack carrying any external twist.
  - Explanation: A nonintegral inertial Kummer exponent forces the entire twisted category to vanish, including with external coefficients.
- **claim-irrational-support-cutoff** (theorem, [source](#stmt-foundations-cutoff)): For $s\notin\mathbb Q$, the category $D_{Y_H}(L(V)^s)$ vanishes on every component of nontorsion degree. There is a quasi-compact open $j:U\hookrightarrow Y_H$, contained in the union of the torsion-degree components, such that $$\label{foundations:cutoff-equivalence} j^!:D_{Y_H}(L(V)^s)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }D_U(L(V)^s)$$ with inverse $j_*$. The same open works for $-s$, and the equivalence persists after taking a product with any spectator stack and any external twist there.
  - Explanation: Restriction to a suitable quasi-compact torsion-degree open recovers the full irrationally twisted category; the result is categorical rather than a statement about support closures.
- **claim-twisted-compact-generation-duality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-foundations-categories)): Let $Y$ be a smooth quasi-compact open in a bundle stack as above, and let $\tau$ be a determinant-line twist. Then $D_\tau(Y)$ is compactly generated. On every smooth finite-type scheme chart, the pullback of a compact object has bounded coherent cohomology. For two such stacks and twists, external tensor product induces an equivalence $$\label{foundations:kunneth} D_{\tau_1}(Y_1)\otimes D_{\tau_2}(Y_2) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } D_{\tau_1\boxplus\tau_2}(Y_1\times Y_2).$$ The ordinary categorical dual of $D_\tau(Y)$ is $D_{-\tau}(Y)$, with evaluation and coevaluation $$\label{foundations:evaluation} (M,N)\longmapsto \Gamma_{\mathrm{dR}}^{\mathrm{ren}}(Y,M\otimes^!N), \qquad \Delta_*\omega_Y.$$ The twist on the diagonal is canonically trivial. These assertions remain valid for the full bundle categories reduced by Proposition <a href="#foundations:cutoff" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="foundations:cutoff">3</a>.
  - Explanation: Supplies compact generation, local coherence, external tensor products, and opposite-twist categorical duality with renormalized evaluation.
- **claim-twisted-pseudoidentity-equivalence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-pseudo-equivalence)): For every $H,V,s$ as above, the functor $F_H$ is an equivalence. The assertion holds on all components, including those on which the twisted category is zero, and also with $s$ replaced by $-s$.
  - Explanation: The extraordinary diagonal kernel defines an equivalence at irrational twist, including zero components and the opposite twist.
- **claim-defect-fiber-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-pseudo-fiber-descent)): Let $i_\theta:S_\theta\hookrightarrow\widetilde Y_P^u$ be a defect stratum, and let $f_\theta:S_\theta\to B_\theta$ be its Levi Hecke-data projection. Its twist is pulled back from $B_\theta$, and there is a locally holonomic complex $K_\theta$ on that base such that $$\label{eq:M2} i_\theta^!J\simeq f_\theta^!K_\theta.$$
  - Explanation: The boundary restriction of the compactified parabolic kernel descends from the Levi Hecke-data base with its induced twist.
- **claim-clean-noncharacteristic-kernel** (theorem, [source](#stmt-pseudo-clean-noncharacteristic)): The kernel $J$ is clean: $j_!\omega\simeq j_*\omega$ in the specified twist. Moreover, on a smooth Levi chart $S\to Y_M^u$, choose a scheme presentation of $\widetilde Y_P^u\times_{Y_M^u}S$ and a local closed embedding into a smooth scheme over $S$. The characteristic variety of the closed direct image of $J$ contains no nonzero covector pulled back from $S$.
  - Explanation: The compactified kernel is clean and has no nonzero characteristic covectors coming from the smooth Levi base.
- **claim-first-parabolic-adjunction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-pseudo-first-adjunction)): On degree $u$, the continuous functor $L_P=E_P[-2e]$ is a left adjoint of $C_P$: $$\label{eq:M1} L_P=E_P[-2e]\ \dashv\ C_P.$$ It computes the partially defined expression $p_!q^*$ on every object.
  - Explanation: The shifted Eisenstein functor gives an actual continuous left adjoint on the entire Levi category.
- **claim-second-parabolic-adjunction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-pseudo-second-adjunction)): On the same torsion component there is an adjunction $$\label{eq:M3} C_{P^-}\ \dashv\ E_P.$$
  - Explanation: The opposite constant term is left adjoint to Eisenstein series on the specified torsion component.
- **claim-pseudoidentity-boundary-factorization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-pseudo-boundary-factorization)): For semisimple $H$, there is a natural transformation $$F_H\longrightarrow\operatorname{Id}[-2\dim Y]$$ whose cone has a finite filtration with quotients factoring through constant term, a functor between Levi categories, and Eisenstein series for proper parabolics.
  - Explanation: The comparison with the shifted identity has a finite cone filtration whose terms pass through proper Levi categories.
- **claim-pole-grassmannian-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-whittaker-model-comparison)): For a connected semisimple complex group $H$, a smooth complete curve $X$, and the fixed half-canonical datum defining $T_0$, the functor $\mu^!$ identifies the pole-model Whittaker category with the strongly $\chi$-equivariant D-module category on $\operatorname{Gr}_{P_0,S}$ with its relative determinant twist. This holds for every exponent $s$, with arbitrary D-modules in the marked-point parameters, and is compatible with the multipoint and Ran presentations. The assertion also holds with both signs reversed.
  - Explanation: Identifies pole and Grassmannian Whittaker models with determinant twists, arbitrary parameter coefficients, and the specified sign and Ran compatibilities.
- **claim-continuous-whittaker-projection** (theorem, [source](#stmt-whittaker-strata-properties)): In every pole bound, inclusion of the strongly Whittaker category has a continuous right adjoint $\operatorname{Av}_*$. Its image consists exactly of the objects $F$ satisfying* 1. *$f_D^!F=0$ on every irrelevant stratum;* 2. *on a relevant stratum, $f_D^!F=\operatorname{Exp}(\psi_D)\otimes^!q_D^!E_D$ for an object $E_D$ in the D-module category of $S_D$ with its induced twist.* *The analogous statement uses $-\psi_D$ for the opposite character. Restriction by $!$ computes the projection on each stratum. These projections commute with $!$-base change in the parameter schemes and with tensoring a spectator category. They are compatible with $!$-restriction between pole bounds. Closed direct images, both between pole bounds and along closed parameter embeddings, preserve the Whittaker subcategories.* *If a bounded-zero open contains every relevant stratum of a pole bound, restriction to that open and star extension identify its Whittaker category with that of the entire bound.
  - Explanation: Constructs continuous Whittaker projection, characterizes it by stratum tests, and establishes parameter, spectator, pole-bound, and closed-image compatibilities.
- **claim-whittaker-opposite-duality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-whittaker-duality)): The categories $\mathcal W_s^+(S)$ and $\mathcal W_{-s}^-(S)$ are dual, with the normalized pairing $$\label{eq:W2} \langle W,W'\rangle= \Gamma_{\mathrm{dR}}(W\otimes^!W')[-2\delta_N].$$ In a pole bound this formula uses the bounded-zero star-extension convention of Proposition <a href="#whittaker:strata-properties" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="whittaker:strata-properties">12</a>. It then extends continuously to the full pole model. Equivalently, one may place one argument in a pole bound and $!$-restrict the other to that bound. The analogous pairing relative to $S$ is defined by relative star image. Closed images transpose to $!$-restrictions.* *These statements hold for the Ran categories, formed as limits under $!$-restriction along the diagonals, and are compatible with tensoring a spectator category.
  - Explanation: Opposite twists and characters are categorical duals under the normalized de Rham pairing, including the full pole and Ran presentations.
- **claim-whittaker-standard-summands** (theorem, [source](#stmt-whittaker-standards)): Suppose $s$ is irrational or zero. Over a fixed coincidence piece $S$, the Whittaker category is the direct sum, in presentable DG categories, of the categories $D(\mathcal L_D^s)$ indexed by relevant labels $D$. The inclusion of the $D$-summand is star extension from its stratum; with the normalization below it is $$\label{eq:W3} E\longmapsto f_{D,*}\bigl(\operatorname{Exp}(\psi_D)\otimes^!q_D^!E[-a_D]\bigr).$$ The construction takes place in any pole bound containing the label and is then carried to larger bounds by closed image. For holonomic arguments in this formula, the canonical shriek-to-star map is an isomorphism. Both assertions hold for the opposite twist and character.
  - Explanation: On a fixed coincidence piece, relevant labels give orthogonal standard summands; holonomic shriek and star extensions agree.
- **claim-whittaker-tstructure-amplitude** (theorem, [source](#stmt-whittaker-t-structure)): This t-structure restricts to each Whittaker pole bound and extends to the full pole model with t-exact closed transition images. With this convention <a href="#eq:W3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:W3">[eq:W3]</a> is t-exact. On an affine chart where a smooth divisor diagonal has inclusion $i$ and affine open complement $j$, $$i_*,\ j^!,\ j_*\quad\text{are t-exact}, \qquad i^!\quad\text{has t-amplitude }[0,1].$$ The resulting t-structures on the parameter categories used here are separated.
  - Explanation: Fixes compatible separated Whittaker t-structures, exact standard embeddings, and the divisor amplitude needed for collision extension.
- **claim-holonomic-fourier-comparisons** (theorem, [source](#stmt-deform-fourier)): On holonomic arguments, the $!$ and $*$ integrals in the axis defining $\mathsf F$ agree canonically. Consequently Fourier commutes with both pullbacks and both direct images for maps independent of the axis, whenever these holonomic operations are defined. These identifications respect adjunctions, the $!$-to-$*$ map, and diagonal orientation maps pulled back from the diagram without the axis.
  - Explanation: Clean Fourier integration permits both kinds of pullback and direct image for axis-independent maps, compatibly with the geometric comparison maps.
- **claim-nontorsion-rank-constancy** (theorem, [source](#stmt-deform-rank)): Consider a finite geometric diagram as above. Assume that its $q$-dependence is introduced by Kummer factors $M_q(r)$ for algebraic invertible functions $r$, and that the corresponding diagrams with these factors recorded as graphs have mixed Hodge origin. At every output stalk, the dimensions of its specialized cohomologies and the ranks of the induced maps are constant as $q$ ranges over complex numbers that are not roots of unity. In particular, a finite output complex which vanishes at $q=1$ vanishes at every such $q$.
  - Explanation: Mixed-origin finite geometric diagrams have constant specialized cohomology dimensions and map ranks away from roots of unity.
- **claim-logarithm-colimit-vanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-deform-colimit)): Let $\{K_i\}$ be a filtered system of finite geometric calculations with outputs on a fixed finite schematic chart. Suppose that each calculation and all transition maps are linear in a single input $M_q(r)$. Assume their substitutions by $\mathcal L_n(r)$ lift to mixed diagrams compatibly with <a href="#eq:logarithm-sequence" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:logarithm-sequence">[eq:logarithm-sequence]</a>. For every stalk $x$ and every degree $d$, suppose that $$\underset{i}{\operatorname{colim}}\, H^d\bigl((K_i)_{x,q=1}\bigr)=0$$ and that the weights of these groups have a common upper bound $C_{x,d}$, independent of $i$. Then the same cohomology colimit vanishes at every non-root-of-unity value of $q$.
  - Explanation: Linearity, compatible logarithm lifts, ordinary-parameter colimit vanishing, and uniform upper weights together transfer vanishing to non-torsion monodromy.
- **claim-regular-holonomic-stalk-detection** (theorem, [source](#stmt-deform-stalks)): On a finite smooth chart, the filtered colimits of regular-holonomic complexes occurring above are detected by constructible stalks. The analogous holonomic Ind-category has a separated perverse $t$-structure and embeds fully faithfully into all $D$-modules.
  - Explanation: Constructible stalks detect the particular regular-holonomic filtered colimits; this is not a detection principle for arbitrary D-modules.
- **claim-finite-whittaker-stage-diagrams** (construction, [source](#stmt-deform-stages)): There is a canonical finite triangle $$\widehat M_{I,m}\longrightarrow\widehat F \longrightarrow\widehat F_\perp$$ such that $\widehat M_{I,m}$ is a finite extension of images of the $\widehat T_\sigma$ and every $\widehat H_\sigma$ kills $\widehat F_\perp$. After field specialization, Fourier transform, and $!$-restriction at $t=1$, its first map is the counit of Whittaker projection of $\pi^!F_W$. Denote that projection by $M_{I,m}$. The augmented stages $$\label{eq:P4} \pi_!\widehat M_{I,m} \longrightarrow F_W\boxtimes\delta_{u=0}$$ form a geometric diagram under increases of pole bounds and closed diagonals of marked parameters. This entire diagram is linear in the single initial Kummer input.
  - Explanation: Builds finite projection triangles and coherent augmented stage diagrams linear in the original Kummer input.
- **claim-transverse-vinberg-map** (theorem, [source](#stmt-deform-transverse-map)): The restriction $p_{2,\mathrm{tr}}$ is representable and separated. On finite output charts the unrestricted $p_{2,*}$ has the unipotent-stabilizer finiteness required for the finite geometric calculus.
  - Explanation: Establishes representability and separatedness on the transverse open and the allowed unipotent-stabilizer calculus for the unrestricted image.
- **claim-finite-vinberg-isomorphisms** (theorem, [source](#stmt-deform-vinberg)): For $s\notin\mathbb Q$ and $D=M_{I,m}$, both arrows in <a href="#eq:P5" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P5">[eq:P5]</a> are isomorphisms. They are natural under the stage transitions, smooth chart changes, and retention of marked parameters. The same conclusion holds for the fixed-point, fixed-label standard Whittaker objects of <a href="#eq:W3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:W3">[eq:W3]</a>.
  - Explanation: The finite geometric comparison arrows become isomorphisms at irrational exponent and remain compatible with stage and parameter changes.
- **claim-finite-whittaker-test** (theorem, [source](#stmt-planch-finite-test)): The functor $\mathcal T_0$ kills the anti-tempered subcategory of $D(Y)$. If $s\notin\mathbb Q$, the functor $\mathcal T_s$ is conservative on all of $D_s$. Both assertions remain valid after tensoring with a spectator D-module category.
  - Explanation: The fixed finite test annihilates the ordinary anti-tempered category and detects all objects at irrational twist, including with spectators.
- **claim-ordinary-tested-colimit-zero** (theorem, [source](#stmt-planch-zero-colimit)): For every stalk $\xi$ on a test chart and every degree $j$, $$\operatorname*{colim}_\beta H^j\bigl((\widehat K_\beta)_{\xi,q=1}\bigr)=0.$$
  - Explanation: Every stalk cohomology colimit of the tested finite cones vanishes at ordinary monodromy.
- **claim-satake-variable-separation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-planch-separation)): After <a href="#eq:P8" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P8">[eq:P8]</a>, the term indexed by $\lambda$, star extended to $\overline S_\alpha$ and pushed by $\pi_!$ with marked parameters retained, is, modulo $u$-constants, $$\mathsf S_\lambda^{(1)}\mathsf S_\lambda^{\prime(2)} \left((U_0*_{!,u}U'_0)\boxtimes (j_\alpha)_*\omega_{S_\alpha}\right). \label{eq:P10}$$ Both Hecke operations are over $\overline S_\alpha$. The second is the transpose-path version of $\mathsf S_\lambda^r$: its path is reversed back to the forward direction, but its kernel is $K_\lambda^r$, rather than $K_\lambda$. Formula <a href="#eq:P10" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P10">[eq:P10]</a> includes the base dualizing factors and has no additional shifts depending on $I$, $\alpha$, or $\lambda$.
  - Explanation: Separates the bundle variables into vacuum inputs and mutually dual Satake kernels, with all parameter dualizing factors retained.
- **claim-global-vacuum-weight-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-planch-vacuum-weight)): The objects $\bar U_0$ and $\bar U'_0$ have fixed upper complex-weight bounds on their entire bundle stacks. In <a href="#eq:P10" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P10">[eq:P10]</a>, omit $(j_\alpha)_*\omega_{S_\alpha}$ and instead use the unshifted constant complex $k_{\overline S_\alpha}$, of weight zero and ordinary degree zero. With the bar inputs, the resulting object has an upper complex-weight bound independent of $I,\alpha,\lambda$ and the pole bound.
  - Explanation: Projected vacuum inputs have global upper weights, and the opposite Satake contributions cancel before configuration integration.
- **claim-uniform-satake-degree** (bound, [source](#stmt-planch-satake-degree)): Fix smooth output charts on the two copies of $Y$. With the bar inputs and the parameter factor $k_{\overline S_\alpha}$ used in Lemma <a href="#planch:vacuum-weight" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="planch:vacuum-weight">26</a>, the star restriction of <a href="#eq:P10" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P10">[eq:P10]</a> to every fibre of $\overline S_\alpha$ has a uniform upper ordinary cohomological degree. The bound includes all tuples of points, all further collisions, and all Satake labels.
  - Explanation: Classical spectral localization supplies an upper ordinary degree bound independent of labels and all collision patterns.
- **claim-uniform-tested-weight-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-planch-weight-estimate)): Fix a test chart, a stalk $\xi$, and a degree $j$. The mixed Hodge structures $H^j((\widehat K_\beta)_{\xi,q=1})$ have a common upper weight bound, independent of $\beta$ and hence of all pole, configuration, label, and skeletal indices.
  - Explanation: Collision and skeletal degree decay leave only finitely many weight regimes contributing to a fixed stalk degree.
- **claim-irrational-plancherel-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-planch-identity)): For $s\notin\mathbb Q$, the natural transformation <a href="#eq:P6" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P6">[eq:P6]</a> is an isomorphism. Consequently $$J_sR_s\simeq\operatorname{Id}_{D_s},$$ as asserted in <a href="#eq:P1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P1">[eq:P1]</a>.
  - Explanation: The Whittaker–Poincaré counit is an isomorphism on the entire irrationally twisted category.
- **claim-relative-invariant-coinvariant-duality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-relative-equivariance)): Let $J\to S$ be one of the smooth affine finite jet groups of the arc, congruence, or unipotent groups used here. Put $A_J=D_*(J)$ and let $\mathbf1_J=D(S)$ be its module given by relative de Rham direct image. For every $D(S)$-linear strong $J$-category $\mathcal E$, the norm calculation identifies $\mathcal E_J$ with $\mathcal E^J$, naturally also in additional coefficient categories. Under this duality:* 1. *geometric relative tensor products over $A_J$ are D-modules on contracted products, with star integration in a free group variable;* 2. *$\operatorname{End}_{A_J}(\mathbf1_J)=D(B_SJ)$, with ! tensor;* 3. *the unbalanced evaluation $$\operatorname{ev}_J: {}_{A_J}\mathbf1_J\otimes_{D(S)}\mathbf1_J{}_{A_J} \longrightarrow A_J$$ has a continuous right adjoint, linear for the left and right $A_J$-actions. Both actions on $\mathbf1_J$ are given by the de Rham augmentation.* *The assertions hold for the pro-smooth groups in use, whose kernels over a finite jet stage are pro-unipotent, and commute with change of smooth parameter base. Character versions use the corresponding exponential and its inverse on opposite sides.
  - Explanation: Strong relative group actions admit invariant–coinvariant identification, contracted-product formulas, and continuous linear evaluation adjoints.
- **claim-harish-chandra-renormalization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-hc-renormalization)): The underlying quasi-coherent categories have the following properties.* 1. *The comparison with the ordinary derived category of smooth Harish–Chandra modules is t-exact and is an equivalence on complexes bounded below in cohomological degrees.* 2. *The category for $(\ell,J)$ is monadic over renormalized $J$-representations, with the PBW induction monad. Its t-structure is created by the forgetful functor.* 3. *The compact-generator mapping calculations commute with smooth affine base change, restriction to smooth closed collision and graph charts, residue fields, and the finite flat scalar extensions used on infinitesimal diagonals. In the last case the generators are perfect relative to the scalar extension.* 4. *Restriction to a smaller compact open with smooth finite-dimensional quotient preserves compact objects. Between pro-unipotent opens it is fully faithful and has a continuous right adjoint.
  - Explanation: Provides bounded-below ordinary comparison, the PBW monad, controlled scalar extensions, and compact-preserving restriction without identifying arbitrary unbounded ordinary categories.
- **claim-formal-diagonal-crystal-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-crystal)): The categories just constructed and their restriction and induction functors descend along the formal diagonal groupoid of $S$. Their sections are $D(S)$-linear categories, with underlying categories as above. The construction commutes with smooth parameter change and with separation into disjoint clusters, including after restriction to a collision locus.
  - Explanation: Comparisons through cofinal deeper levels give coherent infinitesimal transport and crystal categories across collisions.
- **claim-strong-loop-action** (construction, [source](#stmt-loop-strong-action)): Formula <a href="#eq:L1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:L1">[eq:L1]</a>, paired by ! tensor and star integration, defines a unital associative $\mathcal A$-action on $\mathcal M$ in $D(S)$-module categories. For each compact open $J$ used above, its strong $(J,\chi_J)$-equivariant category is the renormalized Harish–Chandra category for $(\ell,J)$ with differential $\operatorname{act}_\ell-\chi_J$. These identifications respect the forgetful maps into $\mathcal M$.
  - Explanation: The conjugation and parameter-derivative formula defines a coherent strong loop action and identifies its compact-open equivariance with corrected Harish–Chandra modules.
- **claim-balanced-pairing-adjoints** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-pairing-adjoints)): At the irrational levels under consideration, the balanced functor $$\overline F_S: C_S\otimes_{\mathcal S_S}d_S\longrightarrow Q_S$$ is fully faithful and has a continuous $D(S)$-linear right adjoint. The projection $C_S\otimes_{D(S)}d_S\to C_S\otimes_{\mathcal S_S}d_S$ also has a continuous $D(S)$-linear right adjoint. These assertions hold over the full parameter scheme, including its collision loci.
  - Explanation: The balanced spherical–Whittaker pairing is fully faithful and both it and balancing have continuous parameter-linear right adjoints across collisions.
- **claim-pairing-parameter-operations** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-parameter-operations)): Let $f:T\to S$ be a change between the smooth affine parameter charts used here, including a principal open or a smooth closed collision or graph chart. For each of the families $\mathcal E=\mathcal M,C,a,d,Q$, there is an identification $$\mathcal E_T\simeq D(T)\otimes_{D(S)}\mathcal E_S.$$ The pairing and its continuous linear right adjoint base change under these identifications. For a smooth closed inclusion $i:Z\to S$ and a principal open inclusion $j:U\to S$, they commute with $i_*,i^!,j_*,j^!$, including the units and counits of the adjunctions.
  - Explanation: The local categories, pairing, adjoints, units, and counits commute with the specified smooth-chart parameter changes and open–closed operations.
- **claim-adolescent-whittaker-presentation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-walg-adolescent)): There is a canonical presentation $$\label{eq:L5} Q_S\simeq\underset{i\geq1}{\operatorname{colim}}P_i, \qquad P_i=\mathcal M^{I_i,\chi},$$ whose transition functors are star averaging with character. They are fully faithful and have continuous $D(S)$-linear right adjoints. After passage to $b$, they preserve compact objects. These assertions hold over collision loci and after the base changes of Section <a href="#sec:loop" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:loop">7</a>. The same presentation and transition assertions apply with $a_S$ in place of $\mathcal M$.
  - Explanation: Presents Whittaker coinvariants by adolescent stages whose character-averaging transitions are fully faithful and admit continuous linear right adjoints.
- **claim-relative-depth-vacua** (construction, [source](#stmt-walg-vacua)): The reduction of the induced $(I_i,\chi)$-generator, calculated with the $N_i$-lattice, is a flat heart module $V_{i,R}^W$. It has a distinguished vector $\mathbf v_i$ with presentation $$\label{eq:L7} w(u^{i d_w}\mathcal O)\mathbf v_i=0, \qquad V_{i,R}^W\text{ has PBW basis in modes of orders }<i d_w.$$ It corepresents vectors satisfying the displayed annihilations. These constructions commute with the scalar extensions used here, including the finite flat infinitesimal tests for the crystal. The ordinary vacuum satisfies the same assertion for $i=0$.
  - Explanation: Relative reduction produces flat cyclic heart modules with PBW presentations and universal annihilation conditions compatible with the allowed scalar extensions.
- **claim-vacuum-ext-continuity-base-change** (theorem, [source](#stmt-walg-ext)): For every depth $i\geq0$ and every $p\geq0$, the functor $\operatorname{Ext}^p_{\mathcal H_R^W}(V_{i,R}^W,-)$ commutes with filtered colimits. If $R\to T$ is a scalar extension occurring in our affine or infinitesimal charts, then, for a smooth $W$-module $M$ over $T$, restriction gives $$\label{walg:restriction-ext} \operatorname{Ext}^p_{\mathcal H_T^W}(V_{i,T}^W,M) \simeq \operatorname{Ext}^p_{\mathcal H_R^W} (V_{i,R}^W,\operatorname{oblv}_R M).$$ For smooth affine or residue-field extensions, and for the finite flat infinitesimal tests, the ordinary derived mapping complexes between depth vacua consequently satisfy $$\label{walg:mapping-base-change} \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal H_R^W}(V_{i,R}^W,V_{j,R}^W) \otimes_R^{\mathbf L} T \simeq \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal H_T^W}(V_{i,T}^W,V_{j,T}^W).$$
  - Explanation: Derived maps from depth vacua commute with filtered colimits and the specified finite-Tor or flat scalar changes.
- **claim-relative-skryabin-equivalence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-walg-relative-skryabin)): Reduction induces an equivalence $$Q_S^0\simeq\mathcal W_R^{\mathrm{ren}}.$$ On compact objects its composite with the ordinary comparison to $D(\mathcal H_R^W)$ is <a href="#eq:L6" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:L6">[eq:L6]</a>. This comparison is fully faithful on compact objects and has essential image $\mathcal V_R^W$. It commutes with the scalar extensions in Lemma <a href="#walg:ext" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="walg:ext">38</a> and with the crystal transport of Section <a href="#sec:loop" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:loop">7</a>.
  - Explanation: Identifies the underlying Whittaker category with renormalized principal W-modules while retaining ordinary maps on compact objects and crystal transport.
- **claim-ordinary-vacuum-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-walg-ordinary-vacuum)): The image in $Q_S^0$ of the spherical Kac–Moody vacuum is compact. Its ordinary comparison is $V_{0,R}^W$. Consequently adjoining $V_{0,R}^W$ to the generators of $\mathcal V_R^W$ does not change that category.
  - Explanation: Geometric pairing adjoints place the ordinary vacuum in the compact image already generated by positive-depth vacua.
- **claim-common-whittaker-crystal-target** (theorem, [source](#stmt-walg-common-target)): For the inverse shifted levels on the two Langlands-dual Lie algebras, there is a canonical identification of the crystal categories $Q_S$. It respects pullback in $S$, collisions of marks, changes of curve coordinate, and exterior products for disjoint clusters. The underlying-complex functors from these categories to $D(S)$ are identified. The ordinary vacuum and its distinguished horizontal generating cycle are identified as well.
  - Explanation: Conformal Feigin–Frenkel duality identifies the relative Whittaker targets, underlying complexes, and horizontal vacuum for inverse shifted levels.
- **claim-spherical-heart-realization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-local-heart)): On the coordinate charts just described, the $t$-structure on $C_S$ is separated and compatible with filtered colimits. Its heart is a Grothendieck abelian category, and there is a continuous equivalence $$\label{eq:L8} D(C_S^\heartsuit)\simeq C_S.$$ The functors $j^!,j_*,i_*$ are $t$-exact when $j$ is a principal open and $i$ is a smooth closed collision diagonal. For a smooth divisor $i$, the functor $i^!$ has amplitude $[0,1]$. These assertions also hold for products of the group categories, with separate subsets of the marks assigned to the different factors.
  - Explanation: The parameter-normalized spherical heart is Grothendieck and its unbounded derived category realizes the separated DG category with the required open–closed amplitudes.
- **claim-unit-insertion-functors** (construction, [source](#stmt-local-insertion)): Insertion of the unit defines $t$-exact functors $C_T\to C_V$ and $d_T\to d_V$. They have continuous $D(S)$-linear right adjoints, commute with parameter operations and disjoint products, and use the vacuum when $T=\varnothing$. On arc-induced modules the first functor is $$\label{eq:L9} \operatorname{Ind}_{j_T}^{\ell_T}W \longmapsto \operatorname{Ind}_{j_V}^{\ell_V}(W\|_{H_V}).$$ Here restriction is along the restriction map on regular arcs.
  - Explanation: Insertion adds vacuum marks through exact functors with continuous linear adjoints, compatible with parameter changes and collisions.
- **claim-point-pairing-gap** (theorem, [source](#stmt-local-point-gap)): The point pairing satisfies $$\label{eq:L10} R\operatorname{Hom}_{Q} \bigl(F(M_\eta,D_\lambda),F(M_{\eta'},D_{\lambda'})\bigr) \simeq \begin{cases} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{dR}}(G),& (\eta,\lambda)=(\eta',\lambda'),\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases}$$ The map induced from the input categories identifies cohomology in degrees at most two. Under the common $W$-module comparison, $F(M_\eta,D_\lambda)$ is the irrational-level simple reduction $T^\kappa_{\eta,\lambda}$, tensored with a one-dimensional vector space. Its essential image agrees with the image for the dual pairing with the two labels exchanged.
  - Explanation: Point pairings have diagonal mapping complexes given by group de Rham cohomology, agree with input maps in low degrees, and match simple reductions with exchanged labels.
- **claim-one-slot-local-family-equivalence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-local-one-slot)): There is a canonical continuous $t$-exact equivalence $$\label{eq:L11} \alpha_S:C_S\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\check d_S, \qquad F_1\alpha_S\simeq F_0.$$ It is $D(S)$-linear and compatible with the parameter operations, disjoint products, and coordinate changes. Exchanging the two groups gives $\check\alpha_S:\check C_S\simeq d_S$. The same statements apply to the simultaneous opposite levels.
  - Explanation: Extends the point comparison to a canonical exact equivalence across collision divisors with coherent parameter and disjoint-product structures.
- **claim-two-slot-insertion-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-local-two-slot)): There is a canonical comparison $G_0\simeq G_1$, where $$\label{eq:L12} \begin{aligned} G_0(A,B)&=F_V\bigl(\operatorname{ins}A, \operatorname{ins}(\check\alpha_U B)\bigr),\\ G_1(A,B)&=\check F_V\bigl(\operatorname{ins}B, \operatorname{ins}(\alpha_T A)\bigr). \end{aligned}$$ It agrees with the disjoint comparison and respects $D(S)$-linearity, coordinate changes, disjoint products, symmetries, and all diagonal operations for merge and repetition of marks. Vacua give the empty inputs. In particular, <a href="#eq:L11" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:L11">[eq:L11]</a> is compatible with ordinary insertion of marks.
  - Explanation: Identifies both inserted local pairings and fixes their vacuum, merge, repetition, symmetry, and coordinate compatibilities.
- **claim-global-period-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loc-period-comparison)): Fix $G$ and its level as in Section <a href="#sec:loop" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:loop">7</a>, and let $T$ be a nonempty tuple over a smooth parameter scheme $S$. There is a natural isomorphism of continuous $D(S)$-bilinear pairings $$\label{eq:T1} \left\langle R_T\Lambda_T(M),W'\right\rangle_S \simeq \int_{V\supseteq T} \operatorname{oblv}_W\!\left( F_V(\operatorname{ins}_{T,V}M, \operatorname{ins}_{T,V}W')\right), \qquad M\in C_T,\quad W'\in d_T.$$ It respects the ordinary and crystalline parameter comparisons, including permutations, repetitions, and diagonal mergers of marks.
  - Explanation: Pairs normalized localized Whittaker coefficients with the Ran-integrated local reduction pairing, preserving full parameter and diagonal structures.
- **claim-level-harish-chandra-comparisons** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loc-levels)): The level Harish–Chandra categories have the compact presentations, continuous functors, and ordinary and crystalline parameter comparisons of Propositions <a href="#loop:hc-renormalization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="loop:hc-renormalization">31</a> and <a href="#loop:crystal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="loop:crystal">32</a>. Restriction between two nonzero levels supported on the whole old tuple is fully faithful when compared through a common deeper level. It preserves compact objects. These comparisons remain valid in the presence of extra markings, including collisions with the old ones.
  - Explanation: Transfers compact presentations and crystal comparisons to level structures, with full faithfulness for nonzero level changes on the old tuple.
- **claim-localization-algebroid-construction** (construction, [source](#stmt-loc-construction)): Localization with level is the continuous functor whose calculation on such a chart is $$\label{eq:T2} \operatorname{Loc}_{G,E}^{\mathrm{lv}}(M)\|_U =\mathscr D_U^s\otimes^L_{U(\mathcal T_U)}M_U, \qquad (v,x)m=v(m)+xm.$$ Here $M_U$ is the module pulled to the framed chart and the enveloping algebra uses the specified central quotient. Omitting the center and twist gives $\operatorname{Loc}_{N,E}^{\mathrm{lv}}$. These functors commute with the parameter operations of Proposition <a href="#loop:crystal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="loop:crystal">32</a>, with pullback between smooth bundle charts, and with the deeper-level comparisons of Lemma <a href="#loc:levels" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="loc:levels">48</a>. At zero level divisor, $\operatorname{Loc}_{G,T}^0$ is $\operatorname{Loc}_T$.
  - Explanation: Defines continuous localization by derived induction over the framed localization algebroid and descends its chart, level, and parameter comparisons.
- **claim-localization-propagation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loc-propagation)): With parameters retained, there are natural isomorphisms $$\label{eq:T3} \operatorname{Loc}_{G,U'}^{\mathrm{lv}}(M) \simeq \operatorname{Loc}_{G,E}^{\mathrm{lv}}( \operatorname{ins}_G M),$$ and the analogous isomorphisms for $N$. They respect transitivity, ordinary and crystalline parameter changes, and deeper levels.
  - Explanation: Insertion of additional marks leaves localization unchanged through natural transitive comparisons, including levels and crystal transport.
- **claim-localization-arbitrary-kernel** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loc-kernel)): There is a natural isomorphism $$\label{eq:T6} \operatorname{Loc}_{G,T}^{\mathrm{lv}}(K\star M) \simeq (\operatorname{pr}_{B_G^{\mathrm{lv}}})_* \left(\operatorname{pr}_Z^!K\otimes^! t_Z^!\operatorname{Loc}_T(M)\right).$$ It is compatible with ordinary and crystalline parameter operations, with deeper levels, and with insertion into $E\supseteq T$. In the last comparison, $K$ is taken by closed direct image to the Grassmannian at $E$.
  - Explanation: Localization of convolution with a finite-bound Grassmannian kernel equals the geometric modification transform with its determinant cancellation.
- **claim-whittaker-averaging-period** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loc-averaging)): For the deep level chosen in Proposition <a href="#loc:kernel" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="loc:kernel">51</a>, Expression <a href="#eq:T7" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:T7">[eq:T7]</a> is naturally isomorphic to $$\label{eq:T8} \operatorname{Per}_{G,T}^{\mathrm{lv}}(K\star M)[-2\delta].$$ The isomorphism respects parameter operations, increases of finite bounds, and deeper-level comparisons.
  - Explanation: Finite-level averaging identifies the Grassmannian Whittaker functional with the normalized exponential unipotent period.
- **claim-unipotent-crystalline-period-map** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-unipotent-period)): For the $N$ Harish–Chandra category there is a natural continuous map $$\label{eq:T10} l^{\mathrm{lv}}[\delta]\otimes B_E^{\mathrm{lv}} \longrightarrow \operatorname{Per}_{N,E}^{\mathrm{lv}}.$$ After shifting by $[-2\delta]$, its source identifies canonically with $l_N[-\delta_N]\otimes B_E^0$. In this normalization the map is a map of crystalline operations, compatible with the parameter base changes, lift comparisons, and deeper-level comparisons of Section <a href="#sec:localization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:localization">10</a>.
  - Explanation: Constant functions on the framed unipotent bundle space induce a continuous crystalline period map with exact determinant and lattice normalization.
- **claim-unipotent-double-quotient-presentation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-unipotent-presentation)): Disk gluing identifies $$\label{eq:T11} B_N=[K_l\backslash L_l/H],\qquad \widetilde B_N=K_l\backslash L_l.$$ For $e_l=\operatorname{rank}(A_l/h)$ and $f_l=\operatorname{rank}k_l$, one has $$\label{eq:T12} \delta=e_l-f_l,\qquad l^{\mathrm{lv}}=\det(k_l)\otimes\det(A_l/h)^{-1}.$$ The character $\chi$ on the presentation induces the function $\psi_0$ on $B_N$.
  - Explanation: Disk gluing gives the unipotent bundle and full-frame quotient presentations together with their dimension, determinant, and character formulas.
- **claim-finite-action-period-normalization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-unipotent-finite-period)): After applying $b$, the finite-action localization satisfies $$\label{eq:T14} \begin{aligned} &(q_N^{\mathrm{lv}})_* \bigl(\operatorname{Exp}(-\psi_0) \otimes^!\mathcal V_l(M[J])\bigr)\\ &\quad\simeq l^{\mathrm{lv}}[\delta]\otimes C^\bullet\!\left(\bar A_l, M[J]\otimes\mathcal O(\bar Z)_{-\chi}\right) \otimes\det(A_l/h)[e_l]. \end{aligned}$$ Functions carry the derivative action of the right translations; the subscript $-\chi$ adds the indicated Lie character. The isomorphism is natural for congruence refinement and for enlargement of the height lattice.
  - Explanation: Relative de Rham cohomology and Lie Poincaré duality identify finite-action periods with function-valued cochains and the required graded determinant shifts.
- **claim-restriction-brst-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-unipotent-restriction)): With the restriction functor of Section <a href="#sec:localization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:localization">10</a>, there is a natural isomorphism of continuous operations $$\label{eq:T15} B_E^0\circ\operatorname{Res}\simeq B_E^0,$$ where the right side denotes the operation on the $G$ input category. Consequently <a href="#eq:T10" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:T10">[eq:T10]</a> also gives the period map for $G$ inputs, with the same parameter and level compatibilities.
  - Explanation: Restriction from the reductive group preserves the continuous full-lattice reduction operation, allowing the unipotent period map to act on reductive inputs.
- **claim-ran-integrated-period-isomorphism** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-ran-integrated-period)): The map <a href="#eq:T16" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:T16">[eq:T16]</a> is an isomorphism for unipotent Harish–Chandra inputs at every intermediate tuple $U\supseteq T$. With $U=T$, it is also an isomorphism for every $G$ Harish–Chandra input whenever the level divisor is a nonzero admissible thickening of the entire tuple $T$. These isomorphisms are continuous, linear over the D-module category of the original parameter scheme, and compatible with insertion, deeper levels, and the parameter comparisons of Sections <a href="#sec:localization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:localization">10</a> and <a href="#sec:unipotent" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:unipotent">11</a>.
  - Explanation: Ran integration upgrades the period map to an isomorphism for unipotent inputs and, at nonzero full old-tuple level, all reductive inputs.
- **claim-ran-principal-part-incidence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-ran-principal-parts)): There is a natural identification $$\label{eq:T17} P_V(J_0)\simeq p_{V,*}i_*i^!\bigl(\mathcal I_X(J_0) \boxtimes\omega_{\mathrm{tuple}}\bigr).$$ Under this identification, forgetting supports is the canonical map $P_V(J_0)\to R\Gamma(X,J_0)[1]$. For every finite list of vector bundles $J_1,\ldots,J_r$ and every old tuple $U$, these maps induce an isomorphism $$\label{eq:T18} \int_{V\supseteq U}\mathop{\bigotimes}\limits_{j=1}^r{}^{!} P_V(J_j) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \bigotimes_{j=1}^r R\Gamma(X,J_j)[1].$$ The assertion includes $r=0$, with the tensor units understood, and is compatible with permutations, shifts, and symmetric powers.
  - Explanation: Incidence support realizes principal-part crystals and their Ran-integrated tensor products as shifted global curve cohomology.
- **claim-semi-infinite-shapiro-period** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-ran-shapiro)): With continuous cochains and the Harish–Chandra convention of <a href="#eq:T13" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:T13">[eq:T13]</a>, there are natural identifications $$\label{eq:T19} \begin{aligned} B_V^{\mathrm{lv}}(\operatorname{Ind}W) &\simeq C^\bullet(h,W),\\ (l^{\mathrm{lv}})^{-1}[-\delta]\otimes \operatorname{Per}_{N,V}^{\mathrm{lv}}(\operatorname{Ind}W) &\simeq C^\bullet\bigl(h,W\otimes \mathcal O(\widetilde B_N)\bigr)\\ &\simeq R\Gamma\bigl(B_N,\operatorname{ev}_V^*W\bigr). \end{aligned}$$ The map <a href="#eq:T10" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:T10">[eq:T10]</a> becomes the cochain pullback induced by $W\to W\otimes\mathcal O(\widetilde B_N)$.
  - Explanation: On induced inputs, semi-infinite reduction and normalized periods become continuous arc cochains, with the period map induced by constant functions.
- **claim-ran-unipotent-evaluation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-ran-unipotent-cohomology)): The evaluation map <a href="#eq:T20" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:T20">[eq:T20]</a> is an isomorphism, with its relative parameter comparisons.
  - Explanation: Evaluation identifies integrated arc cochains with global functions on the unipotent bundle stack, compatibly with relative parameters.
- **claim-ran-restriction-localization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-ran-restriction-localization)): The map <a href="#eq:T21" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:T21">[eq:T21]</a> is an isomorphism.
  - Explanation: Integrated unipotent localization of restricted inserted inputs recovers the pullback of reductive localization.
- **claim-ran-nested-insertion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-ran-two-insertions)): The map <a href="#eq:T23" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:T23">[eq:T23]</a> is an isomorphism.
  - Explanation: Nested insertion through unipotent restriction has the same integrated reduction as direct reductive insertion.
- **claim-ran-bilinear-pairing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-ran-pairing)): For $M\in C$ and $\check M\in\check C$, there is a canonical isomorphism of bilinear forms $$\label{eq:T26} \bigl\langle R_A\Lambda(M),\check\alpha(\check M)\bigr\rangle \simeq \bigl\langle R_{B'}\check\Lambda(\check M),\alpha(M)\bigr\rangle.$$ It is compatible with parameter actions, permutations, and diagonals.
  - Explanation: The global Ran pairings for the dual groups agree after normalized localization and the local label-exchange equivalence.
- **claim-four-localization-quotients** (theorem, [source](#stmt-equivalence-localization)): Each of $L,M',L',M$ is a continuous localization: its right adjoint is fully faithful. Its categorical transpose is therefore fully faithful.
  - Explanation: All normalized localization functors are quotient functors and therefore have fully faithful categorical transposes.
- **claim-coefficient-factorization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-equivalence-factorization)): There are continuous functors $f:A\to(B')^\vee$ and $f':A'\to B^\vee$, with natural isomorphisms $$\label{eq:G2} \begin{aligned} R&\simeq(M')^\vee f,&\qquad (S')^\vee&\simeq fL,\\ R'&\simeq M^\vee f',& S^\vee&\simeq f'L'. \end{aligned}$$ They are uniquely determined, together with these isomorphisms, by <a href="#eq:G1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:G1">[eq:G1]</a> and the fully faithful transposes of localization.
  - Explanation: Fully faithful localization transposes uniquely lift coefficient functors to continuous functors on the opposite bundle duals.
- **claim-global-localization-coefficient-compatibility** (theorem, [source](#stmt-equivalence-compatibility)): The equivalence $\Phi$ has the natural localization and coefficient compatibilities $$\label{eq:G5} \begin{gathered} \begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&,column sep=large,row sep=large] \mathcal C \arrow[r,"L"] \arrow[dr,"e_B(S')^\vee"'] \& A \arrow[d,"\Phi"] \\ \& B \end{tikzcd} \\[1ex] R\simeq(M')^\vee e_B^{-1}\Phi. \end{gathered}$$ They hold with the full Ran family structures: they commute with collisions, insertion of vacua, disjoint products, and the base operations in the local comparison and period construction. The first compatibility uniquely determines $\Phi$, with its specified comparison, on the localization quotient.
  - Explanation: Characterizes the global equivalence through its normalized localization and coefficient comparisons with all Ran family coherences.
- **claim-component-central-character-exchange** (theorem, [source](#stmt-equivalence-sectors)): If a source object has central character $\eta\in X^*(Z_G)$ and component $p\in\pi_1(G)$, its image under $\Phi$ has central character $p$ and component $-\eta$. Thus, writing character first and component second, $$\label{eq:G6} (\eta,p)\longmapsto(p,-\eta).$$
  - Explanation: Exchanges the actual central character and component sectors, with the prescribed sign on the target component.
- **claim-central-torsor-transgression** (theorem, [source](#stmt-equivalence-central)): The equivalence $\Phi$ has coherent natural isomorphisms $$\label{eq:G7} \Phi\tau_Q^!\simeq u_Q^{-1}\otimes\Phi, \qquad \tau_{Q'}^!\Phi\simeq\Phi(u'_{Q'}\otimes-).$$ They are natural on the full groupoids of central torsors and respect their tensor products. They and <a href="#eq:G6" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:G6">[eq:G6]</a> remain valid after the integral determinant transport to the convention of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>.
  - Explanation: Intertwines central translation and transgression tensor actions coherently on full torsor groupoids, including after determinant transport.

        "anchor": "stmt-whittaker-strata-properties",
        "exact_quote": "In every pole bound, inclusion of the strongly Whittaker category has a continuous right adjoint $\\operatorname{Av}_*$.         "anchor": "stmt-whittaker-duality",
        "exact_quote": "The categories $\\mathcal W_s^+(S)$ and $\\mathcal W_{-s}^-(S)$ are dual, with the normalized pairing $$\\label{eq:W2}\n \\langle W,W'\\rangle=\n \\Gamma_{\\mathrm{dR}}(W\\otimes^!W')[-2\\delta_N].$$ In a pole bound this formula uses the bounded-zero star-extension convention of Proposition <a href=\"#whittaker:strata-properties\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"whittaker:strata-properties\">12</a>.         "exact_quote": "Suppose $s$ is irrational or zero.         "exact_quote": "The underlying quasi-coherent categories have the following properties.*\n\n1.  *The comparison with the ordinary derived category of smooth Harish–Chandra modules is t-exact and is an equivalence on complexes bounded below in cohomological degrees.*\n\n2.  *The category for $(\\ell,J)$ is monadic over renormalized $J$-representations, with the PBW induction monad. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Shifted-level twisted bundle category** ([source](#intro:level)): If $h^\vee$ is the dual Coxeter number, set $$\label{intro:level} D_c(\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)) :=D\!\left(L_G^{(c-h^\vee)/(2h^\vee)}\right).$$
- **Langlands dual global form** ([source](#intro:level)): Its Langlands dual $G^\vee$ is defined by the dual of the full root datum, so the global form of $G$ is part of the data.
- **Lacing number** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Let $r$ be the lacing number of $G$: it is $1$, $2$, or $3$ according to the ratio of the squared root lengths.
- **Twisted D-module category** ([source](#pm-h-7)): For a line $L$ on a smooth stack $Y$ and $s\in\mathbb C$, write $D(L^s)$ for the presentable DG category of twisted $D$-modules.
- **Strong Kummer convention** ([source](#pm-h-7)): Equivalently, on the frame torsor of $L$ we impose strong Kummer equivariance with the connection $$\label{foundations:kummer} d-s\,d\log t,\qquad q=\exp(2\pi i s).$$
- **QCA stack** ([source](#foundations:operations)): A QCA stack is a quasi-compact algebraic stack with affine automorphism groups; our stacks are locally of finite type over $\mathbb C$.
- **Safe morphism** ([source](#foundations:operations)): A quasi-compact morphism is safe when the neutral components of the automorphism groups in its geometric fibres are unipotent.
- **Twisted pseudo-identity** ([source](#sec:pseudoidentity)): Consequently the kernel $\Delta_!k_{Y_H}$ defines a continuous endofunctor $F_H$ of $\mathcal C_H$; its existence as a kernel uses that the diagonal is schematic and that $k_{Y_H}$ is locally holonomic.
- **Relevant Whittaker stratum** ([source](#pm-h-19)): A stratum is *relevant* if every $\lambda_y$ is dominant.
- **Whittaker coefficient functor** ([source](#whittaker:coefficient-functor)): We can now define the continuous Whittaker coefficient functor with all its required parameter operations: $$\label{whittaker:coefficient-functor} R_H:D(L_H^s)\longrightarrow\mathcal W_s^+(\operatorname{Ran}).$$
- **Finite geometric calculation** ([source](#pm-h-26)): A finite geometric calculation consists of a finite diagram of bounded algebraically constructible complexes, built by the six operations, cones, and finite totalizations from constant complexes, intersection complexes, and the displayed Kummer factors.
- **Isomorphism modulo axis constants** ([source](#eq:pre-axis-projection)): A comparison whose cone is killed by $C_!^u$ will be called an isomorphism *modulo constants in $u$*.
- **Underlying quasi-coherent category of a crystal** ([source](#pm-h-38)): Its underlying quasi-coherent category is $$\mathcal E^0=\operatorname{QCoh}(S) \otimes_{D(S)}\mathcal E(S), \qquad b:\mathcal E(S)\longrightarrow\mathcal E^0.$$
- **Renormalized Harish–Chandra category** ([source](#eq:L2)): Define the renormalized category for $(\ell,J)$ as the Ind category of the idempotent-complete stable category generated by $$\label{eq:L2} \operatorname{Ind}_{j}^{\ell}(V),$$ where $V$ ranges over algebraic $J$-representations that are vector bundles over $S$.
- **Relative renormalized principal W-module category** ([source](#pm-h-48)): Define the relative renormalized category by $$\mathcal W_R^{\mathrm{ren}}= \operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal V_R^W).$$
- **Principal Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction** ([source](#eq:L6)): The reduction functor on compact Kac–Moody modules is the complex $$\label{eq:L6} \operatorname{DS}_R(M)= C^{\infty/2,h}\bigl(\operatorname{Lie}(LN),M\otimes R_{-\chi}\bigr), \qquad h=\operatorname{Lie}N_0(\mathcal O).$$
- **Normalized localization** ([source](#sec:localization)): For a tuple $T$ over a smooth parameter scheme $S$, write $$\operatorname{Loc}_T:C_T\longrightarrow D(L_G^s\boxtimes\mathcal O_S),\qquad \Lambda_T=\operatorname{Loc}_T\otimes l_N^{-1}[\delta_N].$$
- **Transgression local system** ([source](#pm-h-81)): The resulting class has degree $1+2-2=1$ and defines a rank-one local system $u_Q$ with finite monodromy on $Y_{G^\vee}$: $$[u_Q]=\int_X\bigl\langle[Q]\cup\operatorname{obs}\bigr\rangle.$$

|---|---|---|---|---|
| q-dual-shifted-level | Dual shifted parameter | = | $-\frac1{rc}$ | The lacing number belongs to the specified root datum. |
| q-source-integral-determinant-translation | Source determinant exponent after integral translation | = | $\frac{c-h^\vee}{2h^\vee}+1$ | The source shifted parameter and dual Coxeter number. |
| q-harder-narasimhan-threshold | Unstable-stratum cutoff threshold | = | $\max\{0,2g(X)-2\}$ | The threshold depends on the genus; the vanishing test uses simple-root evaluations of the dominant HN coweight. |
| q-parabolic-relative-dimension | Relative dimension of the parabolic-to-Levi map | = | $(g(X)-1)\dim N_P$ | The equality uses torsion Levi degree and is the same for the opposite parabolic. |
| q-whittaker-pairing-shift | Whittaker duality normalization shift | = | $-2\delta_N$ | The unipotent stack dimension is fixed by the curve and Cartan bundle. |
| q-whittaker-stratum-dimension | Relative dimension of a relevant stratum | = | $\delta_N+a_D$ | The label contribution is the sum of its positive-root pairings. |
| q-divisor-pullback-amplitude | Exceptional pullback t-amplitude | = | $[0,1]$ | The assertion concerns the divisor exceptional pullback. |
| q-relative-dual-satake-weight | Complex weight of the relative dual Satake kernel | = | $-d_\lambda$ | The dual kernel cancels the weight contribution of the forward kernel. |
| q-configuration-link-degree | Upper ordinary degree of the configuration-link restriction | ≤ | $c'-2n$ | Collision codimension and the number of distinct points before further collision. |
| q-configuration-integrated-degree | Upper ordinary degree after configuration integration | ≤ | $E-c'$ | The fixed chart bound is independent of labels; collision codimension lowers the degree. |
| q-unit-cone-gap | Lower cohomological degree of the unit cone | ≥ | $3$ | The gap is established on cells and propagated across collision divisors. |
| q-level-dimension-change | Unipotent dimension at level | = | $\delta_N+m$ | The quotient rank depends only on the fixed level divisor. |
| q-double-quotient-stack-dimension | Dimension of the unipotent bundle presentation | = | $e_l-f_l$ | The difference computes the fixed level stack dimension independently of presentation refinement. |
| q-finite-period-total-shift | Total finite-action period shift | = | $\delta+e_l$ | The presentation dimensions cancel according to the stack Euler characteristic. |
| q-outside-mode-height-filtration | Length of the coefficient-height filtration | ≤ | $i(b-a)+1$ | The finite root-height range bounds the filtration before taking exhaustive colimits. |

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-inertia-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-foundations-cutoff) / [proof](#proof-stmt-foundations-cutoff): Use central determinant weights and inertia vanishing to eliminate nontorsion components and excessively unstable strata, then apply localization over the HN exhaustion. -> A common quasi-compact categorical cutoff for opposite twists and spectators.
- **step-twisted-categorical-foundations** [claim](#stmt-foundations-categories) / [proof](#proof-stmt-foundations-categories): Construct twisted induction through relative algebroids, verify unbounded descent, and check the diagonal evaluation identities on smooth charts. -> Compact generation, local coherence, Künneth, and opposite-twist duality.
- **step-parabolic-cleanness** [claim](#stmt-pseudo-clean-noncharacteristic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pseudo-clean-noncharacteristic): Use principal-part modification fields to prove fiberwise smoothness and Levi descent, then eliminate nonzero defect by irrational inertia. -> Clean kernel with no horizontal characteristic covectors.
- **step-parabolic-adjunctions** [claim](#stmt-pseudo-first-adjunction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pseudo-first-adjunction): Tensor the noncharacteristic clean kernel with coherent generators, extend the adjunction continuously, and verify opposite-parabolic second adjointness by interpolation and triangular identities. -> Actual continuous parabolic adjunctions and pseudo-identity intertwining formulas.
- **step-vinberg-boundary-induction** [claim](#stmt-pseudo-equivalence) / [proof](#pm-h-16): Filter the compactified diagonal boundary through proper Levi correspondences, prove full faithfulness on Eisenstein generators and their orthogonal, and descend the reductive case through the central isogeny. -> Twisted pseudo-identity equivalence for the specified reductive groups.
- **step-whittaker-models-projection** [claim](#stmt-whittaker-strata-properties) / [proof](#proof-stmt-whittaker-strata-properties): Lift the local/global comparison to determinant-frame torsors and stabilize finite unipotent averaging by computing all relevant and irrelevant stratum restrictions. -> Equivalent Whittaker models and a continuous projection compatible with families, spectators, and closed images.
- **step-whittaker-duality-standards** [claim](#stmt-whittaker-standards) / [proof](#proof-stmt-whittaker-standards): Transpose the opposite-character projections under ambient duality, pass through pole and Ran presentations, and use point clean standards to identify family summands. -> Opposite-character duality and standard summands with separated parameter t-structures.
- **step-fourier-mellin-ranks** [claim](#stmt-deform-rank) / [proof](#proof-stmt-deform-rank): Encode characters by translations before Fourier specialization and record Kummer dependence geometrically; quasi-unipotence gives clean Mellin integration and constant non-torsion ranks. -> Compatible Fourier operations and a finite non-torsion rank test.
- **step-logarithm-colimit-test** [claim](#stmt-deform-colimit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-deform-colimit): Use compatible logarithm extensions and strict weights to kill finitely generated completed cohomology under later transitions, then transfer zero ranks to non-torsion parameters. -> Non-torsion colimit vanishing detectable by constructible stalks in the stated Ind-category.
- **step-finite-counit-comparisons** [claim](#stmt-deform-vinberg) / [proof](#proof-stmt-deform-vinberg): Build finite stratum projection triangles, establish transverse-map finiteness, and deform the ordinary Vinberg comparison after removing axis constants. -> Coherent finite-stage counit maps identified with the Whittaker–Poincaré kernel.
- **step-finite-test-ordinary-vanishing** [claim](#stmt-planch-finite-test) / [proof](#proof-stmt-planch-finite-test): Combine Iwahori pullback, adjacent-alcove intertwiners, and residual finite Whittaker averaging; compare with ordinary anti-tempering and use irrational inertia for conservativity. -> A conservative irrational test and zero ordinary tested cohomology colimit.
- **step-satake-separation-bounds** [claim](#stmt-planch-satake-degree) / [proof](#proof-stmt-planch-satake-degree): Separate the diagonal variables into vacuum inputs, cancel opposite Satake weights, and use classical spectral localization to bound cohomological degree independently of representations. -> Global upper vacuum weights and a uniform fiberwise ordinary degree bound.
- **step-uniform-weights-plancherel** [claim](#stmt-planch-identity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-planch-identity): Use configuration-link and skeletal degree decay to obtain uniform stalk weights, apply logarithm colimit vanishing, and remove the conservative finite test. -> The full irrational Whittaker–Poincaré identity.
- **step-relative-loop-foundations** [claim](#stmt-loop-strong-action) / [proof](#proof-stmt-loop-strong-action): Reduce relative invariants to finite-group descent, construct PBW renormalized categories, compare cofinal congruence levels on infinitesimal diagonals, and verify the convolution derivative formula. -> Crystal loop categories with a strong action and identified Harish–Chandra equivariance.
- **step-local-pairing-adjoints** [claim](#stmt-loop-pairing-adjoints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-loop-pairing-adjoints): Identify the irrational spherical category on the unit orbit, construct linear evaluation adjoints through finite and ind-proper presentations, and tensor the resulting fully faithful adjunction with coinvariants. -> Balanced pairing with continuous linear adjoints and all specified parameter operations.
- **step-adolescent-vacua** [claim](#stmt-walg-vacua) / [proof](#proof-stmt-walg-vacua): Present coinvariants by adolescent stages using relative Fourier orbits and the perfect residue pairing, then compare free PBW words with point reduction on every residue field. -> Fully faithful stage transitions and flat relative depth vacua with universal presentations.
- **step-relative-skryabin-target** [claim](#stmt-walg-relative-skryabin) / [proof](#proof-stmt-walg-relative-skryabin): Resolve finite depth differences, bootstrap Ext continuity and scalar extension, compare generator mappings on residue fields, and use geometric pairing adjoints to include the ordinary vacuum. -> Relative renormalized Skryabin equivalence with compact ordinary vacuum and crystal transport.
- **step-common-w-target** [claim](#stmt-walg-common-target) / [proof](#proof-stmt-walg-common-target): Transport homogeneous generating fields under conformal Feigin–Frenkel duality, verify the same depth annihilations, and descend the identified compact categories through crystal comparisons. -> A common Whittaker crystal target preserving underlying complexes and the horizontal vacuum.
- **step-local-hearts-insertion-gap** [claim](#stmt-local-point-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-local-point-gap): Construct the connection-module heart and unbounded realization, prove exact PBW insertion at collisions, and compute the point adjunction monad using group de Rham cohomology and simple reduction. -> Separated realized hearts, exact insertion, matched point labels, and low-degree unit gaps.
- **step-local-collision-equivalence** [claim](#stmt-local-one-slot) / [proof](#proof-stmt-local-one-slot): Propagate unit and cross-pairing gaps across divisor localization triangles, identify boundary epimorphisms, and realize the inverse heart equivalences. -> Canonical one-slot local equivalence with family and coordinate coherence.
- **step-two-slot-insertion-coherence** [claim](#stmt-local-two-slot) / [proof](#proof-stmt-local-two-slot): Construct a pairing-intertwining autoequivalence, identify it with the identity by whole-color translation, and determine diagonal vacuum values using extending highest cycles. -> Coherent two-slot comparison including merge and repetition operations.
- **step-level-localization-geometry** [claim](#stmt-loc-kernel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-loc-kernel): Construct level Harish–Chandra comparisons and localization by algebroid induction, prove propagation with PBW cones, and compare arbitrary finite-bound kernels by formal gauge transfer. -> Localization compatible with levels, insertion, arbitrary Grassmannian kernels, and crystalline parameters.
- **step-finite-unipotent-period-map** [claim](#stmt-prop-unipotent-period) / [proof](#pm-h-68): Identify finite-loop averaging with a level period, present framed unipotent bundles by disk gluing, convert finite-action localization to cochains by Spencer and Poincaré duality, and insert constant functions. -> Continuous normalized crystalline period map, including reductive restriction.
- **step-ran-unipotent-contraction** [claim](#stmt-lem-ran-unipotent-cohomology) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ran-unipotent-cohomology): Realize principal parts by incidence supports, contract their tensor products by relative Ran contractibility, apply continuous Shapiro, and pass from vector groups through the graded bracket deformation. -> Ran-integrated period isomorphism for unipotent inputs.
- **step-ran-reductive-comparison** [claim](#stmt-prop-ran-integrated-period) / [proof](#pm-h-73): Filter restriction and insertion by PBW outside count and root height, contract the resulting principal-part expressions, and compare the nested Ran traces. -> Integrated period isomorphism for all reductive Harish–Chandra inputs in the stated level regime.
- **step-global-period-pairings** [claim](#stmt-loc-period-comparison) / [proof](#pm-h-74): Evaluate on finite Grassmannian tests, cancel all level determinant factors, descend along Whittaker functionals, and integrate independent tuples using the two-slot comparison. -> Full parameter-compatible period pairing and its dual-group Ran identity.
- **step-localization-factorization-global-equivalence** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-equivalence-factorization-2): Apply arbitrary-level localization on the irrational cutoff, factor coefficients through its fully faithful transposes, and use the two group-specific Plancherel identities to produce matching inverse functors. -> The global equivalence at the stated shifted levels with its localization and coefficient characterization.

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-global-equivalence**: The unramified equivalence compares the full twisted categories at dual shifted levels, retaining the specified global forms and every connected component.
- **invariant-categorical-cutoff**: At irrational determinant exponent, restriction to a suitable quasi-compact open is an equivalence of twisted categories; nontorsion-degree components vanish. The same open works for the opposite exponent and with external spectator twists.
- **invariant-nontorsion-ranks**: Finite geometric calculations have constant specialized cohomology dimensions and transition-map ranks away from roots of unity under the specified Kummer and mixed Hodge hypotheses.
- **invariant-colimit-transfer**: Vanishing of the specialized cohomology colimit transfers to every non-root-of-unity parameter when the calculations are linear in the single coefficient input, have compatible logarithm lifts, and satisfy the degreewise uniform upper weight bound.
- **invariant-period-integration**: The localized Whittaker pairing identifies with the relative Ran integral of the local pairing, retaining crystalline parameter comparisons and diagonal mergers.
- **invariant-central-sectors**: The equivalence sends the source central character to the negative target component and the source component to the target central character.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-rational-level-extrapolation**: Extend the global equivalence to rational shifted levels using the same statement. -> The global theorem supplies no equivalence in that regime, and the nonintegral inertia argument cannot be invoked without its numerical hypothesis.
- **anti-set-theoretic-support-cutoff**: Treat categorical restriction to the cutoff open as a statement about closures of supports of underlying complexes. -> The cutoff concerns extraordinary restriction of categories and does not establish the proposed set-theoretic support assertion.
- **anti-finite-rank-colimit-shortcut**: Apply the finite rank test directly to an increasing collection of pole bounds whose colimit vanishes at the ordinary parameter. -> A zero colimit only says that individual classes eventually die; it does not make a finite-stage complex vanish.
- **anti-arbitrary-stalk-detection**: Use constructible stalks as a vanishing test for arbitrary objects of the all-D-module category. -> The supplied stalk-detection argument applies inside the specified regular-holonomic Ind-category.
- **anti-fixed-tuple-period**: Replace the global period by semi-infinite cohomology at a fixed finite set of markings. -> The period comparison requires integration over additional markings.
- **anti-unbounded-ordinary-comparison**: Identify the renormalized Kac–Moody category with the ordinary unbounded derived module category. -> The bounded comparison does not justify that unbounded identification.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The results construct equivalences and coherent functor comparisons between presentable categories on complex bundle stacks, using filtered systems and relative Ran integration. They do not supply a finite input-output procedure whose execution decides the categorical assertions. The source explicitly states: "The integration is essential: semi-infinite cohomology at one fixed finite set is not itself the global period." The colimit test additionally requires compatible mixed logarithm diagrams and a common upper weight bound at every stalk and degree. Finite computations of selected root data or algebraic identities would not verify these categorical hypotheses or certify the global equivalence.
